To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the humor level and camera view of short form videos on mobile social media apps have effects on the viewers' experience and persuasive outcome.
humor and camera view in a mobile short form video app have significant impact on users' psychological responses, which in turn, have significant effect on their technology adoption intention.
humor and camera view influence user experience of watching mobile short form video and the user experience influences technology adoption intent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the psychological responses and technology adoption outcomes of short form videos on mobile social media apps, and it extends HCI theories to short form videos.
the psychological responses and technology acceptance outcomes associated with short-form videos in social media apps.
the effects of mobile short form video app features on the user experience and technology acceptance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the level of humor and the type of camera view in mobile short form videos have different effects on users' psychological responses, and these psychological responses in turn have different effects on user experience and technology persuasion outcomes.

the study demonstrated that mobile social media apps can be used for persuasive purposes, and that humor and camera view are important design elements for improving user experience, and for persuading users to adopt the technology.

the level of humor in a short form video has mixed effects on viewers' user experience, while a first person camera view enhances viewers' user experience of a short form video, and the level of humor and the camera view have a positive impact on viewers' post viewing technology adoption intent, mediated by social presence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
humor and camera view in mobile short form videos on mobile social media apps can be effective to enhance user experience and technology persuasion.

the humor of a mobile short form video and its camera view can affect user experience and technology acceptance, and the social presence is a mediator between the humor level of the video and the technology acceptance.

the use of humor and the camera view in the short form video apps could influence user experience and intention of adopting technology, and the effect of humor on user experience and intention to use is mediated by social presence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
humor can help improve user experience and increase the adoption intent of the technology depicted in short form videos on mobile social media apps.
the use of humor in short-form videos on mobile social media apps can be an effective strategy to improve user experience and persuade new technology adoption.
humor and first person camera view can help improve user experience on mobile short form videos, and that the social presence mediated the effect of humor.
